Hi Evelyn — great to hear, and thanks for the attachment. High level options we typically recommend for Dedicated (to balance cost predictability and cash outflow):

1) Phased commit (3-year example): 20% Year 1 / 40% Year 2 / 40% Year 3 — good for teams that want to limit year-1 spend while securing long-term pricing.
2) Moderate ramp: 30% / 35% / 35% — slightly higher year-1 utilization for faster payback of credits.
3) Aggressive commit (if you want lower unit costs sooner): 40% / 40% / 20% (frontloaded).

Discounting:
- Annual prepay (single-year): up to 8% off list depending on commit size and term length.
- 3-year prepay (paid up front): tiered — 12% at $Xk TPM commit, 16% at $Yk, up to 20% for very large, multi-region pools.

Pilot/canary: we can reserve a 30-day burst pool (pilot) at metered pay-as-you-go for the first 30 days and then convert to credits against Year 1 if you convert. Typical add-on pricing ~ +10% on top of the committed unit rate for the pilot window.

I attached a first-pass SOW with a 20/40/40 proposal and an illustrative pricing schedule (Polaris_Ramp_Schedule_v2.xlsx). Rishi and Marcus are looped in to weigh in on discounting & infra constraints. Would you be available for a 30-minute call Wed or Thu this week?

Best,
Mina

Thanks for the proposal, Mina (and team). A couple of clarifying points from procurement:
- Polaris preference is to pay annually (not full 3-year upfront) but take a guaranteed price lock for 3 years. Is that compatible with Redwood's tiering?
- We'd like an option to add a trial canary of 10% of Year-1 capacity for 30 days before Year-1 billing starts (so we can validate infra).
- On discounts: procurement target is 18% effective discount across the 3 years if we sign a 3-year commitment with annual invoicing. If you can't meet 18% without full upfront, would Redwood accept a 3-year locked price + an early-termination clause with a pro-rated repayment schedule?

Attached a procurement template we use for SOW terms (redlines coming from legal). We need numbers by March 12 to get internal approvals.

Tom

Tom — appreciate the clarity. Short answers and a concrete next step: 
- Annual invoicing with 3-year price lock: yes, we can do annual invoices and honor a locked unit price for the full 36 months. To preserve the economics on our side we require an early-termination repayment schedule (standard pro-rata with a 90-day settlement) — we'll put language in the SOW.
- 10% canary for 30 days before Year 1 billing: OK, we can do that as a convertable pilot; pilot charges will be billed PAYG and credited toward Year 1 once you convert.
- Discounting: we can close to your target. Offer: 3-year commit with annual invoicing, locked unit price, and an effective 17% discount for the proposed 20/40/40 ramp at the mid-tier TPM. If you accept a 50% payment at contract signing and 50% at the start of Year 2, we can move to 18.5%.

I'll update the SOW with the termination schedule and include two payment options (annual invoicing with 17% effective discount, or frontloaded 50%/50% with 18.5%). I'll send a DocuSign draft and the redlined SOW by Monday. Can we schedule a 20-minute call Mon morning to finalize?

Best,
Mina
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
